title: How to Work Abroad from Indonesia: A Complete Guide
summary: Want to work abroad from Indonesia? This complete guide walks you through visas, job hunting, documents, and money tips to land your dream job overseas.
body_markdown:
Let’s be honest. At some point, almost every Indonesian has daydreamed about living and working in another country. Maybe it’s the higher salary, the global experience, or simply the thrill of building a new life somewhere completely different. Whatever your reason, that dream is more achievable than you might think.


The good news? Thousands of Indonesians successfully land jobs abroad every year. The not-so-good news? The process can feel overwhelming if you don’t know where to start. That’s exactly why this guide exists. Whether you’re a fresh graduate or a mid-career professional, here’s everything you need to know about **how to work abroad from Indonesia** , step by step.

##


**Why Working Abroad Is Worth Considering**


Before diving into the how-to, let’s talk about the why. Working overseas isn’t just about earning more money (though that’s a big perk). It’s about building a skill set and perspective that’s genuinely hard to replicate at home.


###


**1. Career Growth and Global Exposure**


International work experience makes your resume stand out, both abroad and back home. Employers everywhere respect candidates who have navigated foreign workplaces and multicultural teams.


###


**2. Higher Earning Potential**


Many countries offer salaries that are significantly higher than Indonesian averages, even for entry-level roles. This can help you save faster, support your family, or invest in your future.


###


**3. Personal Development**


Living abroad forces you to grow. You’ll sharpen your language skills, build resilience, and develop a global network that can open doors for decades to come. You can read more about what that journey feels like in[real stories from Indonesians who’ve lived overseas](https://blog.transfez.com/en/what-it-feels-like-to-study-abroad/) .


##


**Step-by-Step: How to Work Abroad from Indonesia**


Ready to make the move? Here’s a practical roadmap to get you from “thinking about it” to actually packing your bags.


###


**1. Choose Your Target Country and Industry**


Not all countries are equally accessible for Indonesian workers. Some popular destinations include Japan, South Korea, Australia, Germany, the Netherlands, Singapore, and the Middle East. Each has its own demand for workers in specific sectors.


Ask yourself:


- Which industries are hiring in that country?
- Do you meet the language requirements?
- What’s the cost of living compared to potential earnings?
- Are there existing Indonesian communities there?


Narrowing this down early saves you a lot of wasted energy later.


###


**2. Prepare Your Documents Early**


This step trips up a lot of people. Start gathering your documents well before you apply for jobs. Here’s what you’ll typically need:


- A valid *paspor* (passport) with enough validity remaining. If you don’t have one yet, check out[this complete guide on what a passport is and how to get one](https://blog.transfez.com/en/what-is-a-passport-complete-guide/) .
- Certified translations of your academic certificates and transcripts
- A professional CV formatted for international standards
- Reference letters from previous employers
- Police clearance certificate ( *SKCK* )
- Health certificate from an authorized clinic


Start this process at least three to six months before your target departure date. Bureaucracy takes time everywhere, including Indonesia.


###


**3. Research and Apply for the Right Visa**


This is the step most people find most confusing. The type of visa you need depends entirely on what kind of work you’ll be doing and which country you’re going to.


Common work visa categories include:


- **Skilled worker visas** for professionals with specific qualifications
- **Working holiday visas** for younger workers (usually under 30) in countries like Australia and Japan
- **Employer-sponsored visas** where a company in the destination country supports your application
- **Seasonal or contract worker visas** for labor-intensive sectors like agriculture or construction


The visa application process can be lengthy and document-heavy. For a deeper breakdown of the process,[this complete visa guide for beginners](https://blog.transfez.com/en/how-to-get-a-visa/) is a great place to start.


###


**4. Find a Job Before You Leave (When Possible)**


Securing a job offer before you move makes everything easier, including your visa application. Here’s where to look:


- **LinkedIn** : The most powerful tool for professional job hunting internationally
- **Indeed, Glassdoor, and country-specific job boards** : Each country has its own popular platforms
- **BNP2TKI / BP2MI** : Indonesia’s official agency for placing workers abroad. Going through official channels protects your rights as a worker.
- **Company websites** : Apply directly if you have a target employer
- **Recruitment agencies** : Especially useful for blue-collar or hospitality jobs


Tailor your CV and cover letter to fit the norms of your target country. A German employer expects a very different CV format than an Australian one.


###


**5. Improve the Skills That Matter Most**


Two things will significantly improve your chances of landing a job abroad: language skills and recognized certifications.


For language, focus on whatever is spoken in your target country. English proficiency (IELTS or TOEFL) opens doors in most English-speaking countries. Japanese proficiency tests (JLPT) are essential for Japan. German B1 or B2 level is often required for many roles in Germany.


For certifications, look into what credentials are recognized internationally in your field. Engineers, nurses, and tradespeople often need to have their qualifications formally assessed and recognized in the destination country.


###


**6. Understand Your Financial Setup**


Once you’re abroad and earning, you’ll likely want to send money back to family in Indonesia. This is something many overseas workers do regularly, and it’s important to find a reliable, cost-effective way to do it.


Understanding how international bank transfers work, including things like[what a SWIFT code is](https://blog.transfez.com/en/what-is-a-swift-code-complete-guide/) , will help you avoid unnecessary confusion when transferring money. Also, know that apps like Transfez make it straightforward to[send money from abroad to Indonesia](https://blog.transfez.com/en/how-to-send-money-from-abroad-to-indonesia/) without the usual headache of traditional bank transfers.


##


**Common Mistakes to Avoid When Working Abroad**


Learning from others’ mistakes saves you time, money, and stress. Watch out for these common pitfalls.


###


**1. Using Unofficial Recruitment Agents**


Illegal or unregistered recruitment agents are a serious problem in Indonesia. Always verify that any agency is registered with BP2MI. If something feels off or they’re asking for large upfront fees, walk away.


###


**2. Skipping Research on Worker Rights**


Every country has its own labor laws. Before you sign any contract, understand your rights around working hours, leave entitlements, minimum wage (if applicable to your visa category), and contract termination.


###


**3. Underestimating the Cost of Living**


A high salary overseas doesn’t automatically mean you’ll save more. Cities like Tokyo, Amsterdam, or Sydney are expensive. Map out your expected monthly expenses before committing to a move.


###


**4. Neglecting Your Mental Health**


Culture shock and loneliness are real. Build a support network before you go. Connect with Indonesian communities ( *diaspora* ) in your destination city. Many have active WhatsApp groups, social gatherings, and even mentoring for newcomers.


##


**Bonus: International Scholarships as a Gateway**


Not quite ready to jump straight into work? Many Indonesians use international scholarships as a stepping stone. Studying abroad gives you a local credential, language skills, and a professional network in your target country, all of which make it much easier to stay and work afterward. Check out this full guide on[international scholarships for Indonesian students](https://blog.transfez.com/en/international-scholarships-for-indonesian-students/) if that path interests you.

Working abroad from Indonesia is absolutely within your reach. It takes planning, persistence, and a willingness to step outside your comfort zone, but so does anything worth doing. Start with one step today, whether that’s renewing your passport, brushing up on a language, or simply researching which country fits your goals best. The world is hiring, and there’s a place in it for you.
